extracted.intended_audience: Prospective grant applicants to the John Templeton Foundation (individuals and organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required fields for submitting an Online Funding Inquiry (OFI) to the John Templeton Foundation, covering project description, personnel, budget, expenditure-responsibility rules, timelines, and submission mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project term and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A project has a specific start and end date. Generally, projects submitted to the Foundation may have a term of no more than 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project should be scoped with explicit start/end dates and generally not exceed three years unless otherwise specified elsewhere (see ER limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding cycle & calendar adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation accepts OFIs at any time but reviews OFIs at specific times of the year depending upon the size of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must review the Foundation’s grantmaking calendar to select the cycle that best aligns with the request; timing affects review and allowable start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Area selection / triage
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the Funding Area that best aligns with your proposed project; if your project aligns with more than one area or you're unsure, select 'Unsure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting 'Unsure' will route your OFI to be triaged by staff and sent to the internal department best suited to review it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory fields and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer questions as thoroughly and specifically as possible. An asterisk (*) indicates a mandatory response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required fields (marked *) are completed; incomplete mandatory fields will prevent submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Title should clearly, concisely, and in non-technical terms convey the essence of your proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon; use plain language that communicates the core idea succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Summary content & audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what you plan to do, why it is worth doing, and what impact the project will have; written for a general intellectually engaged reader (e.g., a typical New York Times/London Times reader).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good Executive Summary will briefly answer: a) What specific questions will the project help to answer? b) What activities will you carry out? c) Why is this project needed? d) What concrete deliverables will you produce by project end? e) What impact will your project have? Do not include project team, request amount, or project duration in the Executive Summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description detail & format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Description is the longest and most important field; provide a specific, concise, and detailed description of the activities you plan to carry out with the funds requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If special characters/graphs/figures/formatting are required, upload a document and type 'See attached document' in the text field to refer staff to the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the current conditions in the field(s) relevant to the project, identify the problems the project will address, and articulate the specific opportunity the project presents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the gap/opportunity and why the project matters in its field context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs / Deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: List important events and work products that your project activities will generate and which are necessary to make progress toward your proposed Outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear list of concrete outputs (sometimes called 'deliverables') tied to project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (5-year horizon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes are the specific and identifiable changes you expect your Outputs will bring about (or contribute to bringing about) within 5 years of your project’s end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what success would look like; outcomes should be specific and linked to the listed outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for Success
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why your team and/or organization is positioned to be successful in this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe relevant expertise, past accomplishments, institutional support, and structures that enable successful delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Sir John Templeton's philanthropic vision / Donor Intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how your proposed project would advance the philanthropic vision of Sir John Templeton and aligns with his Donor Intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Foundation's Funding Areas page for details; explicitly connect project goals to donor intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to prior Templeton grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the proposed work is similar to or further expands work of an active or closed grant you or your organization received from the John Templeton Foundation, Templeton World Charity Foundation, or Templeton Religion Trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, explain how the proposed project is similar/ builds upon/ furthers/ expands the prior grant and provide Project Title, Grant ID#, Grant Amount, end date, and a very brief synopsis of the prior grant activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Project Start Date constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Project Start Date should be at least 6 weeks after the end of the relevant funding cycle (i.e., the applicant notification date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the grantmaking calendar prior to submitting to ensure the start date complies with review/timeline constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum project duration (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum permissible duration depends on the type of organization: for most U.S. public charities, the Proposed Project End Date must be no more than 36 months beyond the Proposed Project Start Date; for all other organizations and grants to individuals, no more than 33 months beyond the Proposed Project Start Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project scope and milestones within these duration limits; different rules may apply under ER (see ER limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Contact role and change procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Primary Contact manages all communications with the Foundation regarding the funding request; by default the originator of the OFI is the Primary Contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change the Primary Contact and transfer the request to another portal account, email portal support at support@templeton.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Leader (PI) information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Leader is the person who will take overall leadership of the project; may also be the Primary Contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Project Leader differs from the Primary Contact, provide required information and upload the Project Leader's CV/resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Co-Leader information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Co-Leader (Co-Investigator) works alongside the Project Leader in providing leadership; may be absent or may be the Primary Contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, provide required information on the Co-Leader and upload the Co-Leader's CV/resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatedness/conflict disclosure for Project Leader/Co-Leader
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Project Leader or Co-Leader is related to the Foundation as described in Question 15, contact programofficer@templeton.org before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer 'Yes' to the relatedness question if the Project Leader/Co-Leader (or their spouse/family) presently serves as a Trustee, Officer, or staff member of the Foundation. If the person has served on the Board of Advisors or is related to someone who has served/serves on that advisory board, answer 'No'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional personnel listing
rubrics_metrics.description: For each additional personnel already committed to the project, provide full name, disciplinary and organizational affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include consultants, post-docs, presenters, speakers, panelists, or other required roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant history with the Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you or team members came to learn about the Foundation and whether you have previously applied for or received funding or participated in Foundation-sponsored events or discussed the idea with staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose relevant prior interactions with the Foundation to provide context for the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization country selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the country where the organization seeking funding for this project is located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately indicate organizational location to ensure proper processing and applicability of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual applicant declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are seeking funding in your individual capacity (you will sign the grant agreement and funds will be paid to you in your name) and not through an organization, indicate 'Yes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction affects processing and eligibility; be explicit if applying as an individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization naming and department details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the full name of the college or university (do not use abbreviations) and the specific department or center; provide alternative names or translations if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organization responses require further action (text references emailing programofficer), follow instructions; be precise and avoid acronyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure Responsibility (ER) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: ER is required for grants to organizations that are For Profit, not classified as a U.S. Public Charity, or newly formed Public Charity with limited budget/history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your Organization meets these criteria and the request is approved, JTF will operate under Expenditure Responsibility and require Expenditure Responsibility Reports for the grant duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital expenditure threshold and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital expenditures generally include items with an individual value equal to or greater than $5,000 USD (or foreign currency equivalent) and a 'useful life' of more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful life is defined as the time an asset is expected to be functional and fit-for-purpose. If invited to submit a Full Proposal additional ER details will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of capital expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital expenditures examples include: Equipment (vehicles, office equipment, computer equipment, research/lab equipment, dependent equipment used in aggregate), Website (application/infrastructure development, graphics development), Software (software development, apps, databases including front-end/back-end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These illustrative examples clarify what types of purchases are likely to be treated as capital under ER rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is NOT a capital expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Not capital: equipment/website/software expenditures under $5,000 USD or with useful life <1 year; aggregate costs of independent items (e.g., 3 laptops at $2,000 each totaling $6,000); lease costs; website planning/content/operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat these items as capital for ER reporting purposes; consider whether items are solely used for the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: JTF ER-specific limits on project duration and capital
rubrics_metrics.description: JTF has an internal project duration maximum of 33 months for ER grants, which may limit ability to provide funding for capital expenditures with useful life >3 years; capital with useful life exceeding 5 years (e.g., office furniture) may NOT be purchased; buildings and significant building improvements may NOT be purchased with JTF funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan capital requests and useful-life expectations with these restrictions in mind; ER grants face tighter duration and capital restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed currencies for awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation awards and pays grants in sixteen currencies: USD, AUD, CAD, CHF, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, ILS, JPY, MXN, NZD, SEK, SGD, TRY, ZAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify currency correctly on the request; rounding instructions apply (see budget guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request amount and indirect/overhead allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: How much funding are you requesting? The Foundation will approve an added component for overhead/indirect costs of no more than 15% and welcomes lower percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round to the nearest whole currency unit and use numbers only. Keep indirect cost requests ≤15% unless otherwise advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Project Amount definition and Foundation preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Project Amount may be equal to or greater than the Request Amount. The Total Project Amount is the sum of: (a) the Request Amount and (b) funding secured or requested specifically for this project from other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation favors projects where a proportion of required funding has been secured from other sources; round to nearest whole currency unit and use numbers only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Narrative purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: At the OFI stage, the Budget Narrative helps the Foundation determine if estimated project expenses are reasonable and necessary for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a broad overview (narrative or bullet points) of proposed expenses including anticipated amounts and major categories. If invited to Full Proposal, provide more detailed budgeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Funding: what counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Funding can include funds from other philanthropic organizations, in-kind support from employers of project personnel, or donated time of project members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each potential source, the amount secured or requested, and the status of the request to demonstrate co-funding or other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Funding: exclusions (what does not count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Funding does not include costs for equipment not solely used for the proposed project (e.g., an fMRI scanner), costs for activities associated with but not specifically part of the proposed project (e.g., a larger conference that precedes a proposed workshop), or support for activities that will occur before or after the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not count these items as Additional Funding when calculating Total Project Amount or demonstrating co-funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review & submit mechanics and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: This page provides an opportunity to review contents, download a copy, and identify missing fields or fields that exceed character limits. Once submitted the record becomes read-only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all required fields are complete and within character limits, applicants can submit the OFI. Submission is final (read-only) so verify all content before submitting.
